tier_reason: ClickBench is a well-known independent public suite. Its harness (ClickHouse/ClickBench datafusion/, duckdb/, duckdb-parquet/, lib/benchmark-common.sh) runs DataFusion and DuckDB on the same c7a.metal-48xl, and the raw result JSONs re-derive to exactly 9.78s vs 15.70s hot-run sums. It is not A: the harness states DataFusion's build flags but no CPU model, no rustc version and nothing about DuckDB's build.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~1.6x faster than DuckDB on ClickBench hot-run total on c7a.metal-48xl: DataFusion 54.0.0 (single Parquet file) 9.78s vs DuckDB native storage 15.70s, or vs DuckDB querying the same single Parquet file 15.28s (~1.56x); sum of best-of-3 per query; DataFusion is faster on 36/43 queries vs DuckDB-Parquet (derived from page data). Machine-specific: on c6a.metal it is ~1.17x (14.79s vs 17.32s), and on c6a.4xlarge DataFusion is slower (45.57s vs DuckDB 26.25s).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: DataFusion: datafusion-cli 54.0.0 built from source with cargo build --release, CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=true and RUSTFLAGS='-C codegen-units=1'; rustc is whatever stable version rustup installs (not pinned) (ClickBench datafusion/install). DuckDB: official prebuilt CLI from install.duckdb.org; version and flags not stated.
corrections.caveats: The ratio is our derivation from separate ClickBench result files (DataFusion 2026-08-20, DuckDB 2026-05-11), not a single stated figure. The record's 15.70s DuckDB figure is DuckDB's native storage format, while DataFusion reads Parquet; the like-for-like DuckDB-on-single-Parquet run is 15.28s (still ~1.56x). The win only shows on hot runs and many-core machines. Cold-run (first-run) sums favour DuckDB even on c7a.metal-48xl: 173.8s for DataFusion vs 162.8s for DuckDB native and 122.4s for DuckDB-Parquet. On ClickBench's c6a.4xlarge (16 vCPU), DataFusion is ~1.7x slower than DuckDB in total and wins only 5/43 queries. No CPU model is stated, and no compiler or flags are given for DuckDB.

notes: All three sums re-derive exactly from the raw ClickBench JSONs. The claim is accurate as scoped to c7a.metal-48xl, but the original caveat badly understated the reversal: DuckDB wins on the smaller c6a.4xlarge and on cold runs. I added the DataFusion build flags from ClickBench's install script.

tier_reason: db-benchmark is a well-known independent third-party suite, first run by H2O and now maintained by DuckDB Labs. It runs data.table and pandas on the same data with public scripts (datatable/groupby-datatable.R, pandas/groupby-pandas.py), and the report states the CPU model. It is not A: no compiler or flags are stated for the data.table build or the pandas wheel.

corrections.benchmark_url: https://duckdblabs.github.io/db-benchmark/ (current DuckDB Labs continuation, report generated 2026-08-17; raw timings in https://github.com/duckdblabs/db-benchmark/blob/main/time.csv); original 2021 H2O run: https://h2oai.github.io/db-benchmark/
corrections.claimed_speedup: ~3.3x faster than pandas on groupby 'sum v1 by id1' over 100M rows/100 groups: data.table 1.16.99 0.456-0.524s vs pandas 2.2.3 1.525-1.528s in the same 2025-02-10 batch on c6id.metal. Across all 10 groupby questions in that batch, data.table is ~4.2x faster by geometric mean (29.7s vs 150.7s total) and wins 9/10 (derived from page data). The original H2O 2021 run gave data.table 1.14.1 0.863-0.97s vs pandas 1.2.5 2.841-3.021s (~3.3x) in its last batch, 2021-06-30.
corrections.workload: db-benchmark groupby question 'sum v1 by id1' on the 100M-row, 100-group synthetic table G1_1e8_1e2_0_0 (in-memory, two runs per question), plus the other 9 groupby questions on the same data.
corrections.hardware: DuckDB Labs run: AWS c6id.metal, Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C @ 2.90GHz, 128 cores, 250GB (stated on the report page). Original H2O run: node mr-dl11, Intel Xeon E5-2630 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 40 cores, 125.78GB RAM (stated on the report page). The r3-8xlarge in the H2O README is only a setup guide, not the benchmark machine.
corrections.caveats: The original h2oai/db-benchmark is abandoned: its last timing batch was 2021-06-30, not 2021-01-20, and its master branch was last committed 2021-06-09. The duckdblabs/db-benchmark fork is active (commit 2026-09-23) and shows the margin holding against pandas 2.x (~3.3x on this question, ~4.2x geomean across the groupby questions). data.table timings there come from dev builds (1.16.99/1.17.99). pandas has not been re-run since early 2025, and data.table is not the fastest entrant: DuckDB and Polars beat it. data.table loses to pandas on 'max v1 - min v2 by id3' (5.72s vs 5.04s). No compiler or flags are published.

notes: The record's pandas 1.2.4 numbers (2.726/2.882s) are real but come from the 2021-04-29 batch, and its data.table range mixes several May 2021 batches. Hardware was wrong (r3-8xlarge vs the stated Xeon E5-2630 v4 node). I repointed the entry to the maintained DuckDB Labs fork, which confirms ~3.3x against pandas 2.2.3 and refutes the 'likely narrower' caveat. last_commit was pushed_at, and I fixed it to the default-branch commit date.

tier_reason: ClickBench is a well-known independent public suite. Its harness (ClickHouse/ClickBench databend/, duckdb/, lib/benchmark-common.sh) runs Databend and DuckDB on the same c7a.metal-48xl, and the raw result JSONs re-derive to exactly 9.91s vs 15.70s hot-run sums. It is not A: both engines are prebuilt binaries with no compiler or flags stated, and no CPU model is given.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~1.6x faster than DuckDB on ClickBench hot-run total on c7a.metal-48xl: Databend 9.91s vs DuckDB native storage 15.70s (vs DuckDB on single Parquet 15.28s); sum of best-of-3 per query; Databend is faster on 35/43 queries, ~1.75x by geometric mean (derived from page data). Also ~1.63x on c6a.metal (10.65s vs 17.32s). On c6a.4xlarge Databend is slower in total (41.93s vs 26.25s), with roughly equal geomean.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Databend: prebuilt release binary databend-v0.9.53-nightly (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) downloaded by ClickBench databend/install. DuckDB: official prebuilt CLI from install.duckdb.org. No compiler or flags stated for either.
corrections.license: Apache-2.0 (core) + Elastic-2.0 (enterprise code: src/query/ee, src/meta/ee, src/bendsave, ee_main.rs binaries), per the repo LICENSE file
corrections.caveats: ClickBench's Databend entry pins databend v0.9.53-nightly, released 2023-02-26, even for the 2026-09-26 run, so the number reflects a ~3.5-year-old build, not current v1.2.x. Run dates differ (Databend 2026-09-26 vs DuckDB 2026-05-11). The win only shows on hot runs on large machines. Cold-run sums favour DuckDB (184.9s vs 162.8s on c7a.metal-48xl), and on c6a.4xlarge Databend loses in total (41.93s vs 26.25s). No compiler, flags or CPU model are published. Enterprise features are under Elastic-2.0 (non-OSI), hence usability 'mixed'. The separate Databend-vs-Snowflake TPC-H claim (baseline not in list) is weaker than the '3x' marketing headline.

notes: The hot-run sums verify exactly. The notable find is that ClickBench's Databend install script pins a Feb 2023 nightly (v0.9.53), which should be a tag. GitHub reports license NOASSERTION because the LICENSE splits Apache-2.0 core from Elastic-2.0 enterprise directories, so 'mixed' usability is correct. Stars 9,452; last default-branch commit 2026-09-25.
